newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight interbank rate up after payment.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight interbank rate up after payment.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to as high as 7.8 percent from 5.8/6.0 percent previously after an outgo of 500 million ringgit for a 30-day Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said on Wednesday.
Trading was choppy throughout on active participation by both borrowers and lenders, they said.
"The overnight went up to as high as 7.8 then fell back to 6.5. It's now holding at 7.0-7.5," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, interbank rates were generally steady due to the payment for the Bank Negara bill issue.
Dealers said lack of lenders also kept rates steady.
"Some local banks and finance houses remain short of funds and this is preventing the rates from coming off," said another local bank dealer.
Dealers said some foreign banks, which are normally lenders, were also running short.
One-week money remained at 6.80/90 percent, two-week at 7.00/10 and three-week at 7.10/20.
One-month money was at 7.25/30 percent against 7.30/35. Three-month at 7.35/40 percent and six-month at 7.40/45, were both unchanged.

Dealers said that unless Bank Negara calls for new bill or bond issues, rates were likely to be pressured by improving liquidity in the next few days. There will be maturity of a 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue on Thursday and a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Friday.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell across the board but were kept in a tight range amid uncertainty over over the direction of interest rates, futures dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June and September contracts were both down two points to 92.66, or an implied yield of 7.34 percent.
December was down one to 92.66, or 7.34 percent.
